result.summary: This is a narrow residential and institutional street with continuous sidewalks on both sides and heavy on-street parallel parking. While the narrowness of the travel lane likely keeps vehicle speeds low, the lack of marked crossings and the visual obstructions created by parked cars present risks for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street obscures pedestrians, particularly children, from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the block

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Crossings
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks are visible in this segment, which may lead to unpredictable mid-block crossings in an area with a church and residential housing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at the ends of the block to improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers and shorten the crossing distance.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to designate safe crossing points, especially near the church entrance.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement vertical traffic calming measures to maintain low vehicle speeds in this residential and institutional area.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, well-maintained concrete sidewalk adjacent to a large institutional building. Parallel parked cars provide a buffer between pedestrians and the roadway, though no formal crossing points are visible in this mid-block section.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb can block the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross the street mid-block.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line throughout the foreground and middle ground.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near potential crossing points or intersections to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing
interventions.description: Install a marked mid-block crossing with curb extensions to reduce crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility if demand is high for the institutional building.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow urban street with continuous sidewalks on both sides, though they are constrained by utility poles and adjacent parallel parking. While stop signs control the upcoming intersection, there are no marked crosswalks or curb extensions, and parked vehicles likely obstruct sightlines for crossing pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crosswalks
hazards.description: The intersection ahead is controlled by stop signs but lacks painted crosswalks to alert drivers to pedestrian presence.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parking
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corners block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located within the narrow sidewalk, reducing the effective clear width for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the intersection corners to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility by preventing parking at the corner.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, well-maintained concrete sidewalk adjacent to a two-story brick building with a blank frontage. There is a clear curb separating the walkway from the narrow asphalt roadway, but no physical buffer or street furniture is present.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle separation
hazards.description: There is no physical buffer, such as a planting strip or parked cars, between the sidewalk and the travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line in the foreground

hazards.name: Blank frontage
hazards.description: The building facade has few windows and several closed doors, reducing natural surveillance and eyes on the street.
hazards.location_in_image: The brick building wall facing the sidewalk

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Install street trees or large planters to create a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and vehicles.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add street lighting to improve visibility and perceived safety during evening hours.
